answer: The ridge test I would run is Approved community organiser appointment with community council attestation: an appointment the council renews after project audits, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the signal of that gap is the whole defence in one line. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the ripple of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
